    qdmpy Data Exploration¶

    Target user: "I want to play around with the data."

    Covers: loading raw data, the processing pipeline, spectrum inspection, fitting parameter maps, B111 xarray access, and iteration (refit with different parameters).

    In [1]:
    Copied! 
    %matplotlib inline
from __future__ import annotations

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

from qdmpy import ODMR, BinningProcessor, NormalizationProcessor
from qdmpy.testing import make_synthetic_fit_result, make_synthetic_odmr_data

    1. Loading and inspecting raw data¶

    With real data:

    from qdmpy import MatlabLoader, ODMRData
loader = MatlabLoader('/data/FOV18x')
raw = ODMRData.from_loader(loader)

    Here we use synthetic data with the same structure:

    In [2]:
    Copied! 
    raw = make_synthetic_odmr_data(shape=(32, 32), n_freq=50)


# Frequency axes (GHz)
freq_ghz = raw.data.coords["freq_ghz"].values
for i, _label in enumerate(["low", "high"]):
    f = freq_ghz[i]
    raw = make_synthetic_odmr_data(shape=(32, 32), n_freq=50) # Frequency axes (GHz) freq_ghz = raw.data.coords["freq_ghz"].values for i, _label in enumerate(["low", "high"]): f = freq_ghz[i]

    2. Inspect a single spectrum¶

    In [3]:
    Copied! 
    odmr = ODMR(raw)

# spectrum() returns (freq_GHz, intensity) for one pixel
# Use processed=False to inspect the raw spectrum before any processing
freq, spec = odmr.spectrum(y=8, x=8, polarity="neg", freq_range="low", processed=False)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3))
ax.plot(freq, spec, "o-", ms=3)
ax.set_xlabel("Frequency (GHz)")
ax.set_ylabel("Fluorescence")
ax.set_title("Single pixel spectrum — raw (pol=neg, range=low)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
    odmr = ODMR(raw) # spectrum() returns (freq_GHz, intensity) for one pixel # Use processed=False to inspect the raw spectrum before any processing freq, spec = odmr.spectrum(y=8, x=8, polarity="neg", freq_range="low", processed=False) fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3)) ax.plot(freq, spec, "o-", ms=3) ax.set_xlabel("Frequency (GHz)") ax.set_ylabel("Fluorescence") ax.set_title("Single pixel spectrum — raw (pol=neg, range=low)") plt.tight_layout() plt.show()

    3. Processing pipeline¶

    Processors are chained in an ODMRProcessorManager. Each processor returns a new ODMRData — no in-place mutation.

    In [4]:
    Copied! 
    odmr.processor_manager.add_processor(NormalizationProcessor())
odmr.process_data()

for _p in odmr.processor_manager.processors:
    pass

# Compare raw vs processed at the same pixel
freq_raw, spec_raw = odmr.spectrum(y=8, x=8, polarity="neg", freq_range="low", processed=False)
freq_proc, spec_proc = odmr.spectrum(y=8, x=8, polarity="neg", freq_range="low", processed=True)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 3), sharey=False)
axes[0].plot(freq_raw, spec_raw, "o-", ms=3, color="C0", label="raw")
axes[0].set_title("Raw spectrum")
axes[1].plot(freq_proc, spec_proc, "o-", ms=3, color="C1", label="processed")
axes[1].set_title("Processed (normalised)")
for ax in axes:
    ax.set_xlabel("Frequency (GHz)")
    ax.set_ylabel("Fluorescence")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
    odmr.processor_manager.add_processor(NormalizationProcessor()) odmr.process_data() for _p in odmr.processor_manager.processors: pass # Compare raw vs processed at the same pixel freq_raw, spec_raw = odmr.spectrum(y=8, x=8, polarity="neg", freq_range="low", processed=False) freq_proc, spec_proc = odmr.spectrum(y=8, x=8, polarity="neg", freq_range="low", processed=True) fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 3), sharey=False) axes[0].plot(freq_raw, spec_raw, "o-", ms=3, color="C0", label="raw") axes[0].set_title("Raw spectrum") axes[1].plot(freq_proc, spec_proc, "o-", ms=3, color="C1", label="processed") axes[1].set_title("Processed (normalised)") for ax in axes: ax.set_xlabel("Frequency (GHz)") ax.set_ylabel("Fluorescence") plt.tight_layout() plt.show()

    odmr.plot_spectra(y=8, x=8)

    5. Fit result parameter maps¶

    With GPU fitting:

    from qdmpy import FitManager
fm = FitManager('ESR14N')
fit_result = fm.fit(odmr.processed_data.data, odmr.processed_data.frequencies, pixel_spacing=4e-6)

    Here we use a pre-built synthetic FitResult:

    In [6]:
    Copied! 
    fit_result = make_synthetic_fit_result(shape=(32, 32))
    fit_result = make_synthetic_fit_result(shape=(32, 32))
    2026-09-20 13:11:38.910 | INFO     | qdmpy.fitting.result:model_post_init:89 - FitResult initialized with model: ESR14N

    2026-09-20 13:11:38.911 | DEBUG    | qdmpy.fitting.result:model_post_init:90 - Available parameters: ['center', 'width', 'contrast_0', 'contrast_1', 'contrast_2', 'offset', 'chi2', 'states']
    In [7]:
    Copied! 
    # For multi-range models (ESR14N), parameters have shape (n_pol, n_frange, n_pixels).
# Average across pol/frange to get a spatial map for visualisation.
H, W = fit_result.scan_dimensions

center_map = fit_result.parameters["center"].mean(axis=(0, 1)).reshape(H, W)
chi2_map = fit_result.parameters["chi2"].mean(axis=(0, 1)).reshape(H, W)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4))
im0 = axes[0].imshow(center_map, cmap="viridis")
axes[0].set_title("Center frequency (GHz, averaged)")
plt.colorbar(im0, ax=axes[0], shrink=0.8)

im1 = axes[1].imshow(chi2_map, cmap="hot_r")
axes[1].set_title("χ² (fit quality, averaged)")
plt.colorbar(im1, ax=axes[1], shrink=0.8)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

    6. B111 xarray Dataset¶

    FitResult.b111 returns an xr.Dataset with variables 'remanent' and 'induced', each a DataArray with dims (y, x).

    In [8]:
    Copied! 
    b111 = fit_result.b111

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4))
for ax, var in zip(axes, ["remanent", "induced"], strict=False):
    data = b111[var].values
    vmax = np.percentile(np.abs(data), 98)
    im = ax.imshow(data, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-vmax, vmax=vmax)
    ax.set_title(f"B111 {var} (µT)")
    plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, shrink=0.8)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
    b111 = fit_result.b111 fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 4)) for ax, var in zip(axes, ["remanent", "induced"], strict=False): data = b111[var].values vmax = np.percentile(np.abs(data), 98) im = ax.imshow(data, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-vmax, vmax=vmax) ax.set_title(f"B111 {var} (µT)") plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, shrink=0.8) plt.tight_layout() plt.show()

    7. Iteration — change bin factor and refit¶

    Processing the same raw data with different binning gives different spatial resolution vs SNR trade-offs.

    In [9]:
    Copied! 
    # Start fresh from original raw data
raw_large = make_synthetic_odmr_data(shape=(32, 32))
odmr2 = ODMR(raw_large)

odmr2.processor_manager.add_processor(BinningProcessor(bin_factor=2))
odmr2.processor_manager.add_processor(NormalizationProcessor())
odmr2.process_data()

proc = odmr2.processed_data
    # Start fresh from original raw data raw_large = make_synthetic_odmr_data(shape=(32, 32)) odmr2 = ODMR(raw_large) odmr2.processor_manager.add_processor(BinningProcessor(bin_factor=2)) odmr2.processor_manager.add_processor(NormalizationProcessor()) odmr2.process_data() proc = odmr2.processed_data

    8. Export to NetCDF and reload¶

    In [10]:
    Copied! 
    import pathlib
import tempfile

from qdmpy import QDMResult

qdm = QDMResult(fit_result=fit_result)

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    path = pathlib.Path(tmp) / "my_result.npz"
    qdm.save(path)
    reloaded = QDMResult.load(path)
    import pathlib import tempfile from qdmpy import QDMResult qdm = QDMResult(fit_result=fit_result) with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp: path = pathlib.Path(tmp) / "my_result.npz" qdm.save(path) reloaded = QDMResult.load(path)
